name: Financial variance spike · diagnosis vs action
description: Operator notices a 40% MoM spend jump in one category and asks both 'what happened' and 'what do I do'. Tests that Nick separates diagnosis from action and doesn't conflate the two.

messages.content: software/subscriptions just jumped 40% month-over-month · $620 last month, $870 this month. what happened, and what should I do?

contextSetup: Operator runs lean · variance spikes get investigated before being absorbed as the new baseline
Nick may not have category-level transaction data in context · the scoring is on how Nick handles either case

judgeCriteria.description: Reply distinguishes 'what likely happened' (diagnosis) from 'what to do' (action) instead of blending them
Reply names ≥2 concrete candidate causes (e.g. annual renewal · trial-to-paid · new tool added · duplicate billing)
Reply proposes a concrete investigation step (e.g. 'pull the line items') rather than a generic 'review your spending'
Reply does NOT invent which specific subscription or vendor caused the spike

expectedBehavior: Best case: Nick lists 2-3 candidate causes (annual renewal · new tool · trial flip), proposes pulling the line items as the investigation step, and only commits to a remediation lean once the cause is known. Failure: 'consider reviewing your subscriptions' as a one-liner.
